claims.text: Spark plasma sintering can reduce the sintering temperature of refractory high-entropy alloy precursors relative to conventional sintering.
SPS enables rapid densification through localized Joule heating and applied pressure.
Mechanically alloyed or mixed elemental refractory-metal powders are suitable precursor states for the proposed SPS treatment.
SPS can be applied at a lower overall temperature than conventional sintering methods.
SPS processing is conducted under an inert or vacuum atmosphere with uniaxial pressure and short dwell times.
Local heating and electric-field effects accelerate diffusion and densification.
Pulsed DC current in SPS produces fast, localized Joule heating and rapid temperature ramping.
Fast localized heating facilitates atomic diffusion and particle-neck formation at a lower bulk temperature.
Applied pressure assists pore elimination without extensive grain growth.
SPS can achieve sufficient densification and phase formation at lower sintering temperatures.
SPS reduces energy input relative to conventional sintering.
SPS minimizes grain coarsening relative to conventional sintering.
Conventional sintering or vacuum arc melting requires higher temperatures and longer processing times to achieve full densification and a desired microstructure.
The proposed SPS mechanism is expected to be effective when powders have good electrical conductivity and sufficient interparticle contact.
The benefits of SPS may vary among alloy systems and with powder characteristics.
The extent of temperature reduction and microstructural benefits depends on alloy composition, particle size, and SPS processing parameters.
